newsitem.title: USA: Low prices hurt Stone Container Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: Low prices hurt Stone Container Q1 results.

text.p: Stone Container Corp said on Thursday continued low selling prices for its core products, a result of industrywide overproduction, caused a loss in the first quarter ended March 31.
The company said its net loss totaled $96.7 million, or $0.99 a share, compared to net income of $32.4 million, or $0.31, in the first quarter of 1996.

Sales in the period fell to $1.2 billion from $1.3 billion in the corresponding quarter last year. The latest sales figures include about $59 million in retail bag sales that are now reported as part of S&G Packaging, a non-consolidated affiliate of Stone Container, the company said.

In response to the low prices, the company said it will remove a minimum of 350,000 tons of pulp and paper production in the second quarter. The amount is in addition to 97,000 tons taken in the first quarter, Stone Container said.
Company chairman Roger Stone said he forsees a return to more normal market conditions as early as this summer.
Stone Container is a pulp and paper manufacturer.
Its shares closed up 1/8 Thursday at 10.
